Rooftop solar for small consumers in Goa

Summary

The Goa Electricity Department (GED) supplies about 6,50,000 consumers, and most of them are small consumers who pay tariffs below the average cost of supply. Rooftop solar could narrow that gap for the department while cutting bills for households. This brief sets out three options for the state government and estimates what each would need from the budget.

Where things stand

Rooftop systems on homes in Goa produced about 38 MW in 2023, or roughly 4 per cent of peak demand. Uptake has been slow for three reasons: upfront prices are high, net-metering approvals take months, and few installers work outside Panaji and Margao. GED reported 1,240 pending applications in March 2024, and the average wait for net-metering approval was 97 days.

What we recommend

We recommend that the state government adopt a single-window approval process, offer a capital subsidy of 20 per cent for systems up to 3 kW, and publish a list of empanelled installers. Together, these measures could add 60 MW by 2030 at a public cost of about ₹180 crore. GED would recover part of this outlay through lower power purchases during the day, and households would save about ₹9,000 a year on a typical 2 kW system.
